recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if FHIR-I opens a new tracker to narrow or revise the current incomplete definition wording for operations.
issue_request: FHIR-16922 was a Published FHIR-core CodeSystem change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking why IssueType incomplete was a processing error rather than transient and whether no-store specialized it. The accepted resolution moved incomplete to transient and clarified the difference between partial returned information and persistent-store unavailability.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 13993, represented by git commit 98f2e0e4c8254a36babb34941faf5def60266206. That commit moved incomplete from the processing parent to the transient parent in source/operationoutcome/operationoutcome-spreadsheet.xml and updated the no-store and incomplete definitions before the current CodeSystem XML source refactor.
additional_context: OperationOutcome remains in current build scope as an active resource/special resource with FHIR-I ownership and FMM 5 metadata. Current source/operationoutcome/codesystem-issue-type.xml declares hierarchyMeaning is-a and places no-store and incomplete as sibling concepts under transient with distinct definitions. Jira searches found only the seed issue for this clarification, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no contrary community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the authoritative current CodeSystem already reflects the requested structural clarification and no later discovered decision reverses it.
